title: Double-Win NAS: Towards Deep-to-Shallow Transformable Neural Architecture Search for Intelligent Embedded Systems
problem: CNNs in embedded systems face a fundamental trade-off: deeper networks achieve higher accuracy but suffer from poor hardware efficiency, while shallow networks achieve better hardware efficiency but lower accuracy. Current approaches lack automated methods to find architectures that can transform between depths to balance both objectives.
motivation: Embedded intelligence applications require both high accuracy and hardware efficiency, but existing CNN designs force a choice between these conflicting objectives.
method: Double-Win NAS proposes the first deep-to-shallow transformable neural architecture search paradigm that automatically explores network architectures capable of dynamically transforming their depth. The method uses NAS to discover configurations where networks can operate in deep modes for higher accuracy or shallow modes for better hardware efficiency. Designs are evaluated on NVIDIA Jetson embedded systems to validate hardware efficiency improvements.
key_novelty: First deep-to-shallow transformable NAS paradigm enabling networks to dynamically adapt depth while maintaining both high accuracy and hardware efficiency.
contributions: Establishes the first deep-to-shallow transformable NAS paradigm for embedded systems
Automatically explores transformable neural architectures that balance accuracy and efficiency
Demonstrates superiority over state-of-the-art methods on NVIDIA Jetson platforms
primary_theme: Adaptive neural architecture search for embedded efficiency
